display.purpose: Hero name, footer name, section titles, contact title — one or two words at a time, 700 or 900 weight only.

serif.purpose: Hero tagline and About lede — the voice register, paired with italic accent emphasis.

body.purpose: About/Contact sub-copy and any long-form prose, capped ~46ch.

label.purpose: Nav, socials, dates, meta labels, theme toggle — always uppercase and tracked.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default deceleration curve for reveals and transitions.

motion.name: char-roll
motion.purpose: Character-hover link roll (.chr-hover), 0.6s with 28ms per-character stagger.

components.name: Theme Toggle
components.description: Fixed top-right pill button that flips [data-theme] between dark and light; label uses the character-hover roll instead of a color hover.
components.css: .ds-theme-toggle { position: fixed; top: 1.5rem; right: 1.5rem; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 500; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; padding: 0.5em 0.9em; border: 1px solid rgba(242,240,236,0.14); border-radius: 50px; background: #0a0a0a; color: #f2f0ec; } .ds-chr-wrap { position: relative; display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; } .ds-chr-bot { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 100%; transition: transform 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.87,0,0.13,1); } .ds-chr-top { display: block; transition: transform 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.87,0,0.13,1); } .ds-theme-toggle:hover .ds-chr-top, .ds-theme-toggle:hover .ds-chr-bot { transform: translateY(-100%); } .ds-theme-toggle:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #ff3b14; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Project Row
components.description: Borderless list row for a project entry — display-font title, mono-font date, hairline top/bottom borders, group-hover dims siblings.
components.css: .ds-proj-item { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: 1.1rem 0.25rem; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(242,240,236,0.14); border-top: 1px solid rgba(242,240,236,0.14); font-family: 'Druk Wide', sans-serif; font-size: clamp(1.4rem, 3.2vw, 2.1rem); font-weight: 700; color: #f2f0ec; text-decoration: none; transition: opacity 0.3s; } .ds-proj-date { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.8rem; color: #8a8a86; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.03em; } .ds-proj-item:hover { opacity: 1; }

components.name: Project Preview Card
components.description: Small cursor-following preview card shown on project-row hover — the only card surface in the system.
components.css: .ds-proj-card { width: 220px; background: #141414; border: 1px solid rgba(242,240,236,0.14); border-radius: 4px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-proj-meta { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.65rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: #8a8a86; } .ds-proj-card img { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 4/3; object-fit: cover; display: block; }

components.name: Underline Link
components.description: Plain text link with a bottom-border underline as its sole affordance — no button chrome.
components.css: .ds-underline-link { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.85rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.03em; color: #f2f0ec; text-decoration: none; border-bottom: 1px solid #f2f0ec; padding-bottom: 0.15rem; } .ds-underline-link:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #ff3b14; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: The site opens with a literal camera flythrough — CSS-3D rings drifting toward the viewer as they scroll — and that move sets the terms for everything after it: this is a studio you move through, not a brochure you skim. The base is near-black, flat, and unapologetic; type does the shouting (Druk Wide at 900 weight, filling the viewport) while the interface chrome stays deliberately minimal — hairline borders, mono labels, no shadows, no cards-as-default. Depth is real (3D transforms, scroll-scrubbed blur) rather than faked with drop-shadows. This system explicitly rejects the sterile corporate/agency look and the generic dev-portfolio template (uniform card grids, gradient text, bento layouts, tracked-uppercase eyebrows used as decoration). It also refuses to treat any part of the practice — engineering or fine art — as a decorative aside; both get the same full-bleed, large-type treatment.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black flat base, no shadows — depth from hairline borders and real 3D transforms only
Four-role type system, each role locked to a register (display = names/wordmarks, serif = editorial voice, sans = body copy, mono = technical/nav/label)
One accent color used sparingly (rings, italics, selection, hover glow) — never as a fill
Motion is choreographed and scroll-scrubbed (GSAP + Lenis), not just hover-state feedback
Rough-cut, borderless controls (list rows, underline links, one pill toggle) instead of card/button chrome

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Studio Red/Blue never fills a surface and never colors a button. It marks a single word, a hover state, or a scroll-driven glow — nothing structural.

rules.name: The No-Regular-Display Rule
rules.body: --font-display is set to 700 or 900 only, never 400 — Druk Wide has no regular weight, and a lighter synthetic-bold render is worse than picking one of the two real weights.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: There are no box-shadows anywhere in this system. Depth is conveyed by a one-step tonal shift (bg to bg-elevated) or a hairline border only.

dos: Do keep Studio Red/Blue to single words, hover glows, and selection — never a fill or a button background.
Do use the character-hover roll (.chr-hover) for short interactive labels instead of a plain color-change hover.
Do convey depth with a tonal background shift or a hairline border — never a box-shadow.
Do set --font-display to 700 or 900 only; Druk Wide has no 400 weight.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion on every scroll-scrubbed or choreographed animation — full motion stays the default; the fallback only reaches visitors who opted in at the OS level.
donts: Don't default to card grids for content that isn't previewing an image — the project list is borderless rows on purpose.
Don't add drop-shadows, glassmorphism, or any lifted/glowing surface treatment.
Don't use gradient text, tiny tracked uppercase eyebrows above every section, or numbered section markers as decoration.
Don't let the fine-art side of the portfolio read as a smaller or secondary section.
Don't soften the palette toward a safe corporate look — muted pastels, rounded-everything, generic SaaS blue.
